name: Maharai
overview: Maharai was a male warrior noted as the Netophathite and ranked fifteenth among "the thirty," a select group of David's elite men. He is identified as a Zerahite and held leadership over the tenth division during King David's reign. His tribal affiliation is not explicitly stated beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Maharai means "impetuous," reflecting a possible characteristic or reputation. This proper name is recorded in 2 Samuel 23:28 without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Maharai as a descendant of Zerah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 27:13. Beyond this lineage, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maharai's significance lies in his role as one of David's mighty men, specifically as the fifteenth in the distinguished group known as "the thirty." His leadership over the tenth military division underlines his trusted position in David's army. Being a Zerahite and a Netophathite situates him within the broader tribal and regional context of Israel during David's reign.
